title: Collection temperature slopes did not clearly exceed future slopes in four US mosquito samples in 2016-2019 and 2021-2024
abstract: We tested whether the temperature link to mosquito catch was stronger during collection than one week later. Four samples use NEON RELEASE-2026 records and Daymet V4 R1 weather in eastern and western US sites in 2016-2019 and 2021-2024. Final models use 2,344 site-date means from 17,823 traps at 39 sites, including 4,964 traps with no female catch. Models control prior weather, rain in both windows, sampling conditions, site-month and site-year levels and within-month dates. Collection slopes minus future slopes were +0.094, +0.044, +0.025 and +0.252 units per 5 C on a mean log(1 + females per hour) scale. All four adjusted site/year intervals include zero. All planned variants also gave intervals across zero. These records do not establish a repeated excess collection-temperature link or its absence. Four year groups per fit, daily gridded weather, selected sampling dates, changing plot composition and an unaudited curated source limit the test. Future weather is a timing diagnostic, not a way to isolate population size from activity or capture. The package supplies code, figures, source hashes, aggregate checks and a tested external-data rebuild. It tests no air pollution, disease outcome or causal climate-change effect.

display.caption: Collection temperature slope minus the slope one week later. All four adjusted site/year intervals include zero. Units are changes in mean log(1 + females per hour), per 5 C. Dashed intervals use site clusters only. Four year groups per fit limit uncertainty estimation.
Recorded traps with no female catch remain in the analysis. Bars on the right show separate point slopes for collection and future temperature. Figure 1 gives uncertainty for their difference.

citations.reason: Reuses the exact public input manifest and broad sample selection for a new capture-temperature comparison that retains small and empty catches.
Context for a displaced-temperature diagnostic in moth catches. No source records or code from that study are used.
Pinned public mosquito object, curator methods and source license.
Daily weather definitions and leap-year calendar.
Site and year multiway cluster covariance construction. Four year clusters still limit the approximation.
